title: Afroasiatic languages - Wikipedia
text: The Afroasiatic languages (also known as the Afro-Asiatic, Afrasian, Hamito-Semitic, or Semito-Hamitic languages) are a language family (or phylum) of about 400 languages spoken predominantly in West Asia, North Africa, the Horn of Africa, and parts of the Sahara and Sahel. [4]

title: Mbuko language - Wikipedia
text: Mbuko is an Afro-Asiatic language spoken in the canton of Doulek, Méri subdivision, department of Diamaré, and also in parts of the canton of Serawa, Tokombéré subdivision, department of Mayo-Sava, in the Far North Region of Cameroon.

title: Mbuko - accentnetwork.com
text: Mbuko, spoken by around 50,000 people in northern Cameroon, is part of the Chadic branch of the Afro-Asiatic family. It holds cultural importance, especially in traditional ceremonies.
